9Marks
NYN-marks
noun (modern ministry)
From the nine "marks" of a healthy church set out by Mark Dever; mark from Old English mearc, a sign or boundary, as in the historic notae ecclesiae, the marks of the true church.

📖 Biblical Definition

9Marks is the ministry founded by Mark Dever, pastor of Capitol Hill Baptist Church, devoted to recovering the marks of a healthy local church. The nine are: expository preaching; biblical theology; a biblical understanding of the gospel; a biblical understanding of conversion; biblical evangelism; biblical church membership; biblical church discipline; biblical discipleship and growth; and biblical church leadership. This dictionary commends the ministry without reservation on these heads. Each mark is a recovery of plain New Testament order: that the Word be preached by opening the text and pressing its point (Neh 8:8; 2 Tim 4:2); that the gospel of substitution and the new birth not be assumed but stated; that membership be a meaningful covenant of accountable believers, not a roll of names; that discipline, neglected for a century, be restored as Christ commanded (Matt 18:15-17); and that the church be led by a plurality of qualified elders. These are not innovations but the regulative principle applied to congregational life. This dictionary confesses with 9Marks that the local church, rightly ordered under the Word, is the ordinary means by which Christ keeps and grows His people, and gladly commends a ministry that has called many congregations back to that order.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Mark Dever's ministry recovering nine marks of a healthy church, from expository preaching to elder leadership. This dictionary commends it as a faithful application of New Testament church order.

9MARKS, noun. A ministry recovering the marks of a healthy local church: preaching, gospel, conversion, evangelism, membership, discipline, discipleship, and leadership.

Founded by Mark Dever of Capitol Hill Baptist Church.

"So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading" (Neh 8:8).

Restores church discipline and meaningful membership long neglected.

Commended as the regulative principle applied to the ordering of the congregation.

📖 Key Scripture

2 Tim 4:2 — "Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine."

Neh 8:8 — "So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading."

Matt 18:17 — "And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican."

Titus 1:5 — "For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee:"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

9Marks faces no postmodern redefinition; the principle to recover is the ordinary New Testament order of a healthy church that the ministry exists to restore.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. 9Marks is a contemporary ministry, not a contested term, and the principle to recover is the very burden of its work: the health of the local church. For a century much of evangelicalism let membership become nominal, discipline lapse entirely, and preaching drift from the text to the topical. 9Marks calls the church back to "Preach the word" (2 Tim 4:2), to meaningful membership, and to the discipline Christ Himself appointed (Matt 18:15-17).

The nine marks are not a clever program but a summary of plain apostolic instruction. Expository preaching honors the sufficiency of Scripture; biblical conversion guards against false assurance; church discipline guards the purity of Christ's body; plurality of elders follows Paul's charge to Titus (Titus 1:5). This dictionary commends the ministry as a recovery, not an invention, and confesses with it that the ordinary means of grace, ministered in a rightly ordered church, are how the Shepherd keeps His sheep.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name echoes the historic notae ecclesiae, the marks of the true church, applied here to nine features of congregational health.

Mark, Old English mearc, a sign, boundary, or token.

The Reformers spoke of the notae ecclesiae, marks of the true church.

9Marks names nine concrete features of a healthy congregation.

Each is drawn from plain New Testament instruction, not novelty.

The marks together apply the regulative principle to church life.

Usage

"Many pastors restructured their membership process after reading the 9Marks books."

"9Marks has done more than any ministry to recover church discipline in our day."

"The nine marks of 9Marks are simply New Testament church order stated plainly."
